outcomeNote: A dictum with its prooftext; nothing is contested.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: גְּדוֹלָה תְּפִלָּה יוֹתֵר מִמַּעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים, שֶׁאֵין לְךָ גָּדוֹל בְּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים יוֹתֵר מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן לֹא נַעֲנָה אֶלָּא בִּתְפִלָּה. שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַל תּוֹסֶף דַּבֵּר אֵלַי״ וּסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ: ״עֲלֵה רֹאשׁ הַפִּסְגָּה״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Elazar said:» This story proves that «prayer is greater than good deeds» without prayer (Tosafot), as «there was none greater in» the performance of «good deeds than Moses our teacher; nevertheless, his request was granted,» albeit in a limited manner, in his request to enter Eretz Yisrael, «only through prayer,» when God permitted him to climb the mountain and look out over the land. «As,» initially «it is stated: “Speak no more to Me,” juxtaposed to which is: “Go up to the summit of the mountain.”»

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי אלעזר: גדולה תפלה יותר ממעשים טובים
moves.summary: R' Elazar rules that prayer is greater than good deeds: none was greater in good deeds than Moses, yet he was answered only through prayer.
moves.about: God's refusal of Moses' plea, 'Speak no more to Me', adduced as the starting point of the proof

moves.cueHe: שנאמר: ״אל תוסף דבר אלי״ וסמיך ליה
moves.summary: Proof from the juxtaposition of 'Speak no more to Me' and 'Go up to the summit': the refusal is followed by a partial grant, obtained by prayer.
moves.about: the adjacent verse 'Go up to the summit', read by juxtaposition (סמוכין) as Moses being answered, in part, only through prayer
